_doc: Wire schema for the return shapes of sleuth_mcp tool calls. It exists only in the sidecar, and the root sleuth package ships no copy. The audit test is packages/sleuth_mcp/test/schema/mcp_tool_schema_audit_test.dart. mcp_tool_schema.md is the readable version.
notes: The error envelopes describe how the sidecar handlers behave today. Each handler returns ToolCallResult.text(...) with `isError: true` and one text content that carries the message string. The codes in `errors[].code` appear verbatim as the prefix of that text. There is no central typed error class yet, which is known debt.

Passthrough tools call bridge.callExtension and return the ext.sleuth.* envelope unchanged. Each shim is documented on its own so the audit can check its behavior: the get_issues severityAtLeast filter, the compact-issue projection on get_issues and get_snapshot, the get_snapshot default projection and disk handoff, and the launchModeAdvisory stamp.
The nested snapshot and route-session shapes are in mcp_schema.{json,md}. This file documents only how the tools wrap them.

schemaVersion 2 adds the compact-issue projection. By default get_issues and get_snapshot trim each issue to the actionable subset (severity, category, confidence, title, detail, fixHint, stableId, widgetName, routeName, sourceRoute, confidenceReason, rootCauseIds). Pass verbose:true for the full shape of about 22 fields. Compaction removes fields only and keeps the diff key (stableId and severity), so compare_snapshots and check_budgets work on compact snapshots.

Structured content applies to every tool rather than to one tool's shape. A client that negotiates MCP protocol 2025-06-18 or later also gets a top-level `structuredContent` field on every successful tools/call result. It holds the same JSON as the text content block, as an object. Clients on older protocol versions get the text content only. Error results (isError:true) never carry structuredContent. The field is additive and changes no per-tool data, args or errors shape below, so schemaVersion stays 2.

toolAnnotations locks three MCP annotation hints per tool: destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint. readOnlyHint comes from readOnlyTools and is not repeated here. Only non-default hints are listed. openWorldHint is true for tools whose output reflects external or runtime state: the live-app readers get_snapshot, get_issues, get_route_health, explain_issue, diagnose and check_budgets, and list_devices, which lists the host's devices. It is false for self-contained tools: compare_snapshots diffs its input locally, and app_status reports the server's own status. destructiveHint is true for detach_app, because it ends the session and deletes disk-handoff files. Read-only tools omit destructiveHint and idempotentHint, which the spec ignores unless readOnlyHint is false. Annotations are advisory descriptor metadata, not a return or args shape, so schemaVersion stays 2.

serverErrors lists the errors McpServer returns for any tools/call before or around the handler: argument validation against the tool's inputSchema (missing_required_arg, arg_unknown, arg_type_mismatch, arg_enum_violation, arg_min_length_violation) and dispatch failures. They share the per-tool error envelope (isError:true, code as the message prefix) and apply to every tool, so per-tool `errors` lists only handler-level codes. The audit checks every literal error prefix in the handler and server source against these lists.

Batches, reloads and shutdown apply to every tool rather than to one tool's shape. JSON-RPC batches run only in a session that negotiated protocol 2025-03-26, the one version that defines them. The server answers a batch with one array that holds a response per request and none for notifications, and it refuses an initialize inside a batch with -32600. On any other version, or before initialize, it answers a batch with one -32600 error with id null. While hot_reload runs, the server holds tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get and initialize requests until the reload ends, and it answers ping, notifications/cancelled and the list methods at once. On shutdown (stdin closed, SIGINT, SIGTERM or a failed stdout write), a held request does not run and gets a -32603 error whose message starts with The server is shutting down. The server waits at most 10 s for the requests still running, alongside the detach, which is also bounded by 10 s.

Progress and cancellation apply to every tool rather than to one tool's shape. When a tools/call request carries params._meta.progressToken, a tool that reports progress (attach_app) sends notifications/progress frames {progressToken, progress, message} before its response. progress starts at 1 and goes up by one per stage, there is no total, and message is sent only to clients on protocol 2025-03-26 or later. A notifications/cancelled whose requestId names an in-flight tools/call cancels it, and the server sends no response for that request. attach_app stops and releases what it started, and other tools finish with their response dropped. An unknown or finished requestId is ignored.

The audit checks that the descriptors and toolAnnotations agree. It does not check that a hint matches what the handler does. For example, a destructive tool marked non-destructive passes as long as the descriptor and this doc agree. Hint values are a judgment that a person reviews against the MCP ToolAnnotations spec and the handlers; no test verifies them.

serverErrors.doc: a tool without its own deadlines exceeded the generic tool timeout (--tool-timeout, 10 s by default), or one app call exceeded the bridge's shorter per-call timeout; the connection to the app is kept, so the client retries or calls diagnose

the app's session changed: it answered from a different sessionUuid than the one the bridge follows (a hot restart, or another app at the same URI), or a hot restart replaced the isolate the bridge calls. Reported once: the bridge then follows the new session, so calling the tool again works; after a restart that replaced the isolate it first waits, up to the per-call timeout, for the new main isolate to register ext.sleuth.diagnose. When the bridge could not read the new session, it keeps the old baseline, the message says so, and the next call reports the change again. When the change closed the connection, the message says to call attach_app or connect instead
no app is connected, or a connect is still running or was refused; the message says to call attach_app or connect

too many earlier calls to the app are still unanswered (8 by default), so the bridge did not send this one; the connection is kept. Retry in a few seconds, or call attach_app or connect if the app stays busy

data._doc: Passes ext.sleuth.diagnose.data through and adds two sidecar keys (sidecarVersion, sidecarBuiltAgainstSleuth), plus launchModeAdvisory on a degraded session. Every ext.sleuth.diagnose key stays present.

launchModeAdvisory.presence: when connectionMode is warmup or disconnected, or basic with vmConnected false, which means the VM-only detectors are off; the basic text suggests reopening the app and names DDS as one possible cause. A basic session with vmConnected true gets none.

sections.doc: Sections to include; forwarded to ext.sleuth.snapshot as a comma-joined string. Each item must be one of itemValues, the app's SnapshotSection keys. Omit (or pass an empty list) for the default set, which leaves out the per-frame and raw sample sections.

full.doc: Return every section, including the per-frame and raw sample sections the default leaves out. Cannot be combined with sections.

maxIssueCount.doc: Keep the first N issues in the app's ranked order. The app applies this cap to currentIssues.

maxRouteCount.doc: Keep the N routes with the latest startedAt.

diskHandoff.doc: When true, the sidecar writes the envelope to a temp file, with every section unless sections is set. The tool then returns {path, sizeBytes, sha256, _projectedSections?, _projectionLimits?, _projectionApplied?} instead of inline data.

verbose.doc: When false, the default, the sidecar trims each data.currentIssues entry to the compact actionable subset. true returns every issue field. It changes the field shape only and is independent of the maxIssueCount cap, which the app applies either way.

shims.name: default_projection
shims.doc: An inline call that names no sections and does not pass full:true asks the app for the default set: frameStatsSummary, currentIssues, widgetHeatMap, recurrenceTrends, sessionSummary, startupMetrics and routeSessions. The per-frame and raw sample sections (capturedFrames, recentFrames, recentRequests, heapSamples, phaseEvents, gcEvents, platformChannelEvents) are left out: on an iPhone 12 capturedFrames and recentFrames alone were about 90 % of a 260 KB snapshot, and every success result carries the JSON twice for 2025-06-18 clients (text plus structuredContent). The app stamps the usual projection metadata (_projectedSections, _projectionApplied by_app), and the sidecar adds data._omittedSections and data._omittedSectionsHint. An app that ignores the projection gets the same cut applied by the sidecar, stamped _projectionApplied by_sidecar_fallback. Two default snapshots carry the same _projectedSections, so compare_snapshots accepts them, and the default set holds every section compare_snapshots and check_budgets read. A diskHandoff call without sections writes every section.

shims.name: compact_issues
shims.doc: Unless verbose:true, the sidecar trims every data.currentIssues entry to the compact key set (severity, category, confidence, title, detail, fixHint, stableId, widgetName, routeName, sourceRoute, confidenceReason, rootCauseIds), copying only keys that are present. It runs on both the inline and the disk-handoff path and builds a fresh map, so the bridge envelope is never changed. It does nothing when `sections` left out currentIssues, or when currentIssues is absent or not a list. It keeps stableId and severity, so compare_snapshots and check_budgets still work on compact snapshots.

shims.name: disk_handoff
shims.doc: When `diskHandoff` is true, the sidecar writes the snapshot envelope to a per-process file, Directory.systemTemp/sleuth_snapshot_<pid>/<random>.json, whose name is 128 random bits from Random.secure. It creates the per-pid dir with mode 0700 and the file with mode 0600, and checks both with FileStat. On POSIX, if it cannot set and confirm owner-only permissions, it deletes the file and returns a `disk_handoff_failed` error. POSIX modes do not apply on Windows. The payload can hold mildly sensitive data, such as query tokens in recentRequests[].url, which is why a permission failure stops the handoff. The tool returns {path, sizeBytes, sha256} plus any projection metadata instead of the inline `data` block. The sidecar deletes the files on detach_app and at shutdown, and each new write removes files older than 30 minutes from the process's own dir. Each process has its own dir, so one sidecar never removes another's files. Detach and shutdown also remove the per-pid dir once it is empty. After the shutdown cleanup the sidecar writes no new file, so a get_snapshot still running at exit returns disk_handoff_failed instead, and a call the client cancelled before the write writes nothing. At startup the sidecar removes empty sleuth_snapshot_<pid> dirs that earlier processes left, when they are older than 30 minutes. In a non-empty one whose process is gone, which happens after a sidecar crashed or was killed, it deletes the .json files older than 30 minutes and then the dir once it is empty. It checks the process through /proc on Linux and `ps -p` on other POSIX hosts, and not on Windows. When `diskHandoff` is false or absent, the envelope comes back inline. Lineage fallback: if the app predates projection support and the caller requested a projection (sections, maxIssueCount or maxRouteCount), the sidecar stamps `_projectionApplied: by_sidecar_fallback` on the disk-handoff path. On the inline path it returns `projection_unsupported_by_app` instead, because the full payload would overflow the response cap.

data._doc: Passthrough of ext.sleuth.snapshot.data; the sidecar adds launchModeAdvisory on a degraded session, and _omittedSections plus _omittedSectionsHint on a default call.

launchModeAdvisory.presence: stamped in data on a degraded session (connectionMode warmup or disconnected, or basic without a live VM link). It warns that the snapshot is incomplete because the VM-only detectors are off. On the disk-handoff path it is in the written file.

_omittedSections.presence: when the default projection applied (no sections, no full:true, no diskHandoff); always the seven per-frame and raw sample sections, whether or not the app had data for them

_omittedSectionsHint.presence: with _omittedSections; says to pass full:true or name the sections

errors.doc: full:true was combined with a non-empty sections list
ext.sleuth.snapshot returned an error envelope; the tool returns it inline and never writes it to disk
ext.sleuth.snapshot: a `sections` token is not a known SnapshotSection. Through tools/call the server's enum check rejects an unknown section first with arg_enum_violation
ext.sleuth.snapshot: maxIssueCount or maxRouteCount is not a non-negative integer
ext.sleuth.snapshot: a cap targets a section omitted from `sections`

the caller requested a projection (sections, maxIssueCount or maxRouteCount), but the app runs a sleuth version older than 0.35, which has no projection. The full inline payload would overflow the response cap. Request again with diskHandoff:true, or upgrade the app.

diskHandoff:true, but the sidecar could not restrict the temp dir or file to owner-only permissions, could not write the file, or is shutting down and already deleted its handoff files. Nothing is written.

diskHandoff:true and the client cancelled the request before the snapshot was written, so nothing was written; the server sends no response for a cancelled request, so only direct callers of the handler see it

route.doc: An empty string counts as absent.

maxIssueCount.doc: Keep the first N issues of the app's ranked order, after the severity filter. 0 means no cap, and a negative value is rejected with arg_invalid_int. The cap applies whether or not verbose is set.

verbose.doc: When false, the default, the sidecar trims each kept issue in data.issues to the compact actionable subset. true returns every issue field. It changes the field shape only, so the maxIssueCount cap still applies.

data._doc: Passthrough of ext.sleuth.issues, then trimmed to the compact fields and capped. data.issues entries carry the compact key set unless verbose:true. The sidecar stamps _truncated and _totalCount on data only when the cap dropped at least one issue.

vmConnected.doc: passed through from ext.sleuth.issues data.vmConnected, the app's own VM link (the same flag diagnose reports)

_truncated.presence: stamped true only when maxIssueCount dropped at least one issue from data.issues

_totalCount.presence: the issue count after the filter and before the cap; stamped with _truncated

severityAtLeast.presence: echo stamped only when the severity filter was applied

launchModeAdvisory.presence: stamped in data when connectionMode is warmup or disconnected, or basic with no VM service link; warns the issue list is incomplete because the VM-only detectors are off. See the launch_mode_advisory shim for where the VM flag comes from.

shims.name: severity_filter
shims.doc: When `severityAtLeast` is `warning` or `critical`, the sidecar keeps only the `data.issues` entries whose severity meets the threshold, and adds `data.severityAtLeast` with the requested level. `ok` applies no filter but is echoed the same way. When `severityAtLeast` is absent there is no filter and no echo.

shims.name: compact_projection
shims.doc: After the optional severity filter, the sidecar keeps the first maxIssueCount entries of data.issues in the app's ranked order. The default is 50, and 0 means no cap. Unless verbose:true, it then trims each kept entry to compactIssueKeys, copying only the keys that are present. When the cap dropped any issue, data gains `_truncated:true` and `_totalCount`, the count after the filter and before the cap. Error envelopes, which have no `data` map or no `issues` list, pass through unchanged.

shims.name: launch_mode_advisory
shims.doc: Adds data.launchModeAdvisory on a degraded session: connectionMode warmup or disconnected, or basic with vmConnected false. The flag is data.vmConnected, which apps on sleuth 0.37 and later send. For an older app the sidecar first reads ext.sleuth.diagnose on the same session and uses its data.vmConnected. The issues call runs second and its errors are never swallowed, so a session change between the two calls fails the tool call (session_changed when the bridge sees a new sessionUuid) instead of pairing two sessions. A session_changed or version_skew_* error from the diagnose read also propagates. A diagnose read that fails or takes longer than 2 seconds drops the advisory, and basic with no readable flag gets none.

errors.doc: maxIssueCount is negative (or non-integer); only 0 disables the cap
ext.sleuth.issues returned an error envelope; the tool passes it through unchanged

route.doc: An empty string counts as absent.

errors.doc: ext.sleuth.routeHealth returned an error envelope; the tool passes it through unchanged

data._doc: Passthrough of ext.sleuth.explain.data. Reads live app state: sleuth 0.37+ fills the route, widget and count text from the first live issue matching the stableId (else its canonical family), with neutral wording when none is live; sleuth 0.36 apps return the raw placeholders ({widgetName}, {routeName}, {count}).

errors.doc: the stableId arg is missing or empty; the tool checks it before it calls the app
ext.sleuth.explain returned `unknown_stable_id`; the tool passes it through unchanged
